results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. Additionally, the lobes are further divided into compartments such as α, β, γ1, γ2, and γ4.

results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
There are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. These include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t, and claw-count classes. VFB's ontology places 7 direct subtypes under [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), 22 subtypes in all across 2 levels. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to various brain regions through neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals. VFB records show [266](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, including [larval antennal lobe picky local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111694 "Open larval antennal lobe picky local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") and [adult olfactory receptor neuron Ir75d ac1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110011 "Open adult olfactory receptor neuron Ir75d ac1 in Virtual Fly Brain"). results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain") contains approximately 32,388 neurons, according to FlyWire reports. VFB has annotated [9413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the adult central brain.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- ~32,388 neurons (Whole adult brain, both optic lobes and ocellar ganglia included. Ventral nerve cord NOT included; neurons crossing the neck connective are truncated at the brain boundary. Subcount: fully in central brain. One female adult. Dataset: FlyWire connectome neurons, v783.) — [Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07558-y "Open Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518 via DOI (new tab)")

_FlyWire reports 32,388 neurons FULLY CONTAINED in the central brain out of 139,255 in the whole brain. Neurons that arborise in the central brain but also elsewhere are not in that subcount, so it is a lower bound on 'neurons in the central brain', not a census of them._

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

Reference: [How many neurons are in the fly brain?](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/concepts/neuron-counts/ "Open “How many neurons are in the fly brain?” — Virtual Fly Brain documentation (new tab)")

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviors. The ellipsoid body, fan-shaped body, protocerebral bridge, paired noduli, and the asymmetric body are also referred to as the five core central complex structures. VFB holds [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") records of neurons with some part in [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") and [362](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex") records of neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. It detects looming stimuli, which elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic. VFB holds various records related to LPLC2, including its connectivity, images, and transgene expression data.

results.response:

Its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and there is one of these cells per hemisphere.

The giant fiber neuron has downstream connectivity to [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") classes, with the strongest specific targets including [mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053153 "Open mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult efferent neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051964 "Open adult efferent neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB3-3 lineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048874 "Open NB3-3 lineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult IN18B034 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20010307 "Open adult IN18B034 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [peripherally synapsing interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007408 "Open peripherally synapsing interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult premotor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051437 "Open adult premotor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047106 "Open Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult IN06B008 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20009235 "Open adult IN06B008 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). results.response:
The connectome data indicates that [visual system neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047736 "Open visual system neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to several neuron types that could mediate a connection between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). The strongest specific targets of visual system neuron include [adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 061](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20002119 "Open adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 061 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 106](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20002164 "Open adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 106 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult vest neuron 049](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20003515 "Open adult vest neuron 049 in Virtual Fly Brain").

VFB records show that there are neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body, including [larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111675 "Open larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval uniglomerular projection neuron 67b](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111684 "Open larval uniglomerular projection neuron 67b in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111716 "Open larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB's documentation states that MBON-γ1pedc>α/β, MBON-γ4>γ1γ2, and MBON-β1>α are GABAergic and glutamatergic MBON cell-types that send axons into the MB lobes.

It is plausible that there is a multi-step pathway between the visual system and the mushroom body, as adult visual projection neurons have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This suggests that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these connections.

results.title: Concepts: confidence values

Each study defines its own scale and its own threshold for calling a prediction, so a value should be read against the publication it came from rather than compared across datasets. Virtual Fly Brain does not compute these scores and does not set a cut-off: a low-confidence prediction is displayed with its score rather than hidden.

results.title: API: integrations
results.question: How do I explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons using Navis or pymaid?
results.response:
To explore Virtual Fly Brain neurons, you can use the navis package in Python. First, load an example neuron using `navis.example_neurons(1, kind='skeleton')`. Then, you can access various properties of the neuron, such as its ID, nodes, and cable length, using attributes like `n.id`, `n.nodes`, and `n.cable_length`. You can also use methods like `n.reroot()` to reroot the neuron and `n.plot2d()` or `n.plot3d()` to visualize it. For working with multiple neurons, you can create a NeuronList using `navis.NeuronList(n)` or `navis.example_neurons(5)`, and then access and manipulate the neurons in the list using various methods and attributes.

```
import navis
n = navis.example_neurons(1, kind='skeleton')

n.id
n.nodes
n.cable_length
```
